questions.question: If tanθ + cotθ = 4, then find the value of tan 2 θ + cot 2 θ.
questions.questionHtml: If tanθ + cotθ = 4, then find the value of tan<sup>2</sup>θ + cot<sup>2</sup>θ.
questions.solution:
Given

tanθ + cotθ = 4

Formula used

\((a+b)^2=a^2+b^2+2ab\)

tanθ=1/cotθ

Calculation

tan2θ + cot2θ=(tanθ + cotθ)2-2tanθ × cotθ

⇒ 42 - 2 = 14

∴ The value of tan2θ + cot2θ is 14.

questions.question: If sec 2θ = cosec (θ – 36°), where 2θ is an acute angle, find the value of θ.
questions.questionHtml: If sec 2θ = cosec (θ – 36°), where 2θ is an acute angle, find the value of θ.
questions.solution:
sec 2θ = cosec (θ – 36°) ⇒ sec 2θ = sec (90° – θ + 36°) 

⇒ sec 2θ = sec (126° – θ) ⇒ 2θ = 126° – θ ⇒ θ = 42°

questions.question: If 0 ≤ θ ≤ 90°, and sec 107 θ + cos 107 θ = 2, then, (sec θ + cos θ) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If 0 ≤ θ ≤ 90°, and sec<sup>107</sup> θ + cos<sup>107</sup> θ = 2, then, (sec θ + cos θ) is equal to:
questions.solution:
sec107 θ + cos107 θ = 2

Put θ = 0°

⇒ sec107 0° + cos107 0° = 2

⇒ 1107 + 1107 = 2

⇒ 1 + 1 = 2

⇒ 2 = 2 (satisfied)

Now,

sec θ + cos θ

⇒ sec 0° + cos 0°

⇒ 1 + 1

⇒ 2

questions.question: If sin 2 θ = 2 sin θ - 1, 0° ≤ θ ≤ 90°, then find the value of \(\rm \frac{1 + cosec \theta}{1 - \cos \theta}\)
questions.questionHtml: If sin2 θ = 2 sin θ - 1, 0° ≤ θ ≤ 90°, then find the value of \(\rm \frac{1 + cosec \theta}{1 - \cos \theta}\)
questions.solution:
Given:

sin2 θ = 2 sin θ - 1

0° ≤ θ ≤ 90°

Concept used:

(a - b)2 = a2 - 2ab + b2

Calculation:

sin2 θ = 2 sin θ - 1

⇒ sin2 θ - 2 sin θ + 1 = 0

⇒ (Sin θ - 1)2 = 0

⇒ (Sin θ - 1) = 0

⇒ Sin θ = 1

⇒ θ = 90°

Now,

Cos 90° = 0

Cosec 90° = 1

Now,

\(\rm \frac{1 + cosec \theta}{1 - \cos \theta}\)

⇒ (1 + 1) / (1 - 0)

⇒ 2

∴ The required value of \(\rm \frac{1 + cosec \theta}{1 - \cos \theta}\) is 2.

questions.question: If 7 cot P = 24, then find sin P.
questions.questionHtml: If 7 cot P = 24, then find sin P.
questions.solution:
Given:

7 cot P = 24

Formula used:

In Right-angle triangle

cotθ = \({Base\over Perpendicular}\)

sinθ = \({Perpendicular\over Hypotenuse}\)

Calculation:

In Δ ABC

⇒ By Pythagoras theorem

⇒ AB2 = 242 + 72

⇒ AB2 = 576 + 49 = 625

⇒ AB = √625 = 25

Now, sin P = \({7\over25}\)

∴ The required result will be \({7\over25}\).

questions.question: In a △ABC right-angled at C, if tan A = √3, then the value of sin A cos B cot(A + B) is:
questions.questionHtml: In a △ABC right-angled at C, if tan A = √3, then the value of sin A cos B cot(A + B) is:
questions.solution:
tan A = √3, tan A = a/b = √3, a = √3b, c = √(a2 + b2) = 2b


sin A = a/c = √3/2, cos B = b/2b = 1/2, A + B = 90º, cot(90º) = 0

sin A × cos B × cot(A + B) = (√3/2) × (√3/2) × 0 = 0

questions.question: If b cos θ = a, then cosecθ + cotθ = _________.
questions.questionHtml: If b cos θ = a, then cosecθ + cotθ = _________.
questions.solution:
cos θ = a/b = Base/Hypotenuse, so, Perpendicular = √(b2 - a2)

Then, cosec θ = b/√(b2 - a2) and cot θ = a/√(b2 - a2)

Now, cosecθ + cotθ ⇒ \(\frac {b}{\sqrt {b^2 - a^2}}\) + \({{\frac {a}{\sqrt {b^2 - a^2}}}}\) ⇒ \(\frac {a + b}{\sqrt {b^2 - a^2}}\) ⇒ \(\frac {a + b}{\sqrt {(b -a)(b + a)}}\) ⇒ \(\sqrt {\frac {(a + b)^2}{{(b -a)(b + a)}}}\) ⇒ \(\sqrt{\frac{b+a}{b-a}}\)

questions.question: If 3 sec 2 θ + tan θ = 7, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of \(\frac{{cosec2\theta + cos\theta }}{{sin2\theta + cot\theta }}is:\)
questions.questionHtml: If 3 sec2 θ + tan θ = 7, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of \(\frac{{cosec2\theta + cos\theta }}{{sin2\theta + cot\theta }}is:\)
questions.solution:
3 sec2 θ + tan θ = 7

⇒ Put θ = 45

⇒ 3 sec2 45 + tan 45 = 7

⇒ 3 × 2 + 1 = 7

⇒ 7 = 7 (satisfied)

Now,

⇒ (cosec 2θ + cos θ)/(sin2θ + cot θ)

⇒ (cosec 90 + cos 45)/(sin 90 + cot 45)

⇒ (1 + 1/√2)/(1 + 1)

⇒ (√2 + 1)/2√2

⇒ (2 + √2)/4

questions.question: If \(\cot \theta = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}\) , 0° < θ° < 90°, then the value of \(\frac{{2 - {{\sin }^2}\theta }}{{1 - {{\cos }^2}\theta }} + (cose{c^2}\theta - {\sec} \theta )\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If \(\cot \theta = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}\), 0° < θ° < 90°, then the value of \(\frac{{2 - {{\sin }^2}\theta }}{{1 - {{\cos }^2}\theta }} + (cose{c^2}\theta - {\sec} \theta )\) is:

Given:

\(\cot \theta = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}\)

θ = 60°

Calculation:

 sin 60° =\(\frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{2}\)  

 cos 60° = \(\frac{1}{2}\)

 cosec 60° =\(\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\)

 sec 60° = 2 

substituting the value in the given expression  

 = \(\frac{2-\frac{3}{4}\ }{1-\frac{1}{4}}+(\frac{4}{3}\ -2)\) ⇒\(\frac{\frac{5}{4}\ }{\frac{3}{4}}-\frac{2}{3}\)

 = \(\frac{{5\;}}{3} - \frac{2}{3} = 1\)

∴ the value for the \(\frac{{2 - {{\sin }^2}\theta }}{{1 - {{\cos }^2}\theta }} + (cose{c^2}\theta - {\sec} \theta )\) = 1

questions.question: The value of sec 4 θ(1 - sin 4 θ ) - 2tan 2 θ is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of sec4 θ(1 - sin4 θ) - 2tan2 θ is:
questions.solution:
Given:

sec4 θ(1 – sin4 θ) – 2tan2 θ

Formula used:

1 – sin2θ = cos2θ 

Calculation:

sec4 θ(1 – sin4 θ) –  2tan2 θ

⇒ 1/cos4θ [1 – (sin2θ)2 ] – 2 × sin2θ/cos2θ 

⇒ 1/cos4θ(1 + sin2θ) (1 – sin2θ) – 2sin2θ/cos2θ 

⇒ 1/cos4θ × cos2θ (1 + sin2θ) – 2sin2θ/cos2θ 

⇒ (1 + sin2θ)/cos2θ – 2sin2θ/cos2θ 

⇒ (1 + sin2θ – 2sin2θ)/cos2θ 

⇒ (1 – sin2θ)/cos2θ 

⇒ cos2θ/cos2θ 

⇒ 1

∴ The required value is 1

Shortcut Trick

We can also put θ = 45° 

⇒ sec445°(1 - sin445°) - 2tan245° 

⇒ (√2)4[1 - (1/√2)4] - 2(1)

⇒ 4[1 - 1/4] - 2

⇒ 3 - 2

⇒ 1

questions.question: If sin(A + B) = 1 and cos(A - B) = \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) , A + B ≤ 90° and A > B, then the value of \(\frac{5 \sin^2 B + 4 \tan^2 A}{2 \sin B\cos A}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If sin(A + B) = 1 and cos(A - B) = \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), A + B ≤ 90° and A > B, then the value of \(\frac{5 \sin^2 B + 4 \tan^2 A}{2 \sin B\cos A}\) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

sin(A + B) = 1 and cos(A - B) = √3/2

A + B = 90° and A > B 

Formula used:

sin90° = 1

cos30° = √3/2

sin30° = 1/2

tan60° = √3

cos60° = 1/2

Calculation:

sin(A + B) = 1

⇒ sin(A + B) = 90° 

⇒ A + B = 90° ....(1)

Again, 

cos(A – B) = √3/2

⇒ cos(A – B) = 30° 

⇒ A – B = 30° .....(2)

Adding equation (1) and (2), we get

⇒ A + B + A – B = (90° + 30°)

⇒ 2A = 120° 

⇒ A = (120/2)

⇒ A = 60° 

Putting the value of A in equation(2), we get

⇒ 60° – B = 30° 

⇒ B = 30° 

Now,

\(\frac{5 \sin^2 B + 4 \tan^2 A}{2 \sin B\cos A}\) = (5 × sin230° + 4 tan260°)/(2 × sin30° × cos60°)

⇒ [5 × (1/2)2 + 4 × (√3)2]/(2 × 1/2 × 1/2)

⇒ [(5 × 1/4) + (4 × 3)/1/2]

⇒ [(5/4 + 12)/1/2] 

⇒ [(5 + 48)/4/(1/2)]

⇒ (53/4)/(1/2)

⇒ 53/2

⇒ 26\(\frac{1}{2}\)

So, the required value is \(26\frac{1}{2}\)

questions.question: If sec θ - tan θ = 3, then cos θ is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If sec θ - tan θ = 3, then cos θ  is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given :

Sec θ - tan θ = 3 

Formula used :

Sec2 θ - tan2 θ = 1 or (sec θ - tan θ) × (Sec θ + tan θ) = 1

Calculations :

(sec θ - tan θ) (sec θ + tan θ) = 1

sec θ + tan θ = 1/3      ....(1)

sec θ  - tan θ = 3      ....(2) (given)

Solving equ (1) and (2) 

⇒ Sec θ = 10/6 = 5/3

⇒ cos θ = 3/5 (cos θ = (1/sec θ) 

∴ Cos θ = 3/5

questions.question: \(\left[\frac{\operatorname{cosec} 31^{\circ}-\sec 59^{\circ}}{\left(\sin 18^{\circ} \div \cos 72^{\circ}\right)} \times \frac{\tan 26^{\circ}}{\cot 64^{\circ}}\right]+\left[\frac{\tan 30^{\circ}+\tan 15^{\circ}}{\left(1-\tan 30^{\circ} \tan 15^{\circ}\right)}\right]\) = ______.
questions.questionHtml: \(\left[\frac{\operatorname{cosec} 31^{\circ}-\sec 59^{\circ}}{\left(\sin 18^{\circ} \div \cos 72^{\circ}\right)} \times \frac{\tan 26^{\circ}}{\cot 64^{\circ}}\right]+\left[\frac{\tan 30^{\circ}+\tan 15^{\circ}}{\left(1-\tan 30^{\circ} \tan 15^{\circ}\right)}\right]\) = ______.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Simplify the first part

(cosec 31° - sec 59°) = (1 / sin 31°) - (1 / cos 59°)

sin 18° ÷ cos 72° = sin 18° ÷ sin 18° = 1

tan 26° / cot 64° = tan 26° / tan 26° = 1 ⇒ First part = 0

Step 2: Simplify the second part

tan 30° = 1/√3 ≈ 0.5774 = tan 15° ≈ 0.2679

(tan 30° + tan 15°) / (1 - tan 30° × tan 15°) = (0.5774 + 0.2679) / (1 - (0.5774 ×

0.2679))

⇒ Second part = 1 ⇒ Final answer = 0 + 1 = 1

questions.question: The value of \(\frac{\sec \theta \ cosec \theta}{2+\tan^2 \theta+\cot^2 \theta}\) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\frac{\sec \theta \ cosec \theta}{2+\tan^2 \theta+\cot^2 \theta}\) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{\sec θ \ cosec θ}{2+\tan^2 θ+\cot^2 θ}\)

Concept Used:

(tan θ + cot θ)2 = 2 + tan2 + cot2 θ

Calculation:

(sec θ cosec θ)/(2 + tan2 + cot2 θ)

Using formula:

(sec θ cosec θ)/((tan θ + cot θ)2)

= \(\frac{\frac{1}{cos θ × sin θ}}{\frac{sin^2θ + cos^2 θ}{ sin^2θ × cos^2θ}}\)

= sinθ cosθ/(1)2

= sinθ cosθ

Shortcut Trick Formula Used:

1 + tan2θ = sec2θ 

1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ

Calculation 

In the denominator, we can write,

⇒ 1 + tan2θ + 1 + cot2θ

⇒ sec2θ + cosec2θ

⇒ 1/cos2θ + 1/sin2θ 

⇒ (sin2θ+cos2θ)/(sin2θ × cos2θ) 

⇒ 1/(sin2θ × cos2θ) 

⇒ sec2θ × cosec2θ

Now using the numerator as well, 

⇒ \(\frac{\sec θ \ cosec θ}{ sec^2θ × cosec^2θ}\)

⇒ \(1\over{secθ × cosecθ}\) 

= sinθ cosθ

 ⇒[ (7/3) + 2]/[(7/3) - 2]  ⇒ 13/1 =13

questions.question: The value of (1+ cot A – cosec A)(1 + tan A + sec A) – 1 is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of (1+ cot A – cosec A)(1 + tan A + sec A) – 1 is:
questions.solution:
[(1 + cot A – cosec A)(1 + tan A + sec A)] - 1

⇒ [(1 + (CosA/SinA) – 1/SinA)(1 + (SinA/CosA) + 1/CosA)] - 1

⇒ [(SInA + CosA – 1)/SinA)(CosA + SinA + 1)/CosA)] - 1

⇒ [(SinA + CosA)2 – 12)/CosASinA] - 1

⇒ [(Sin2A + Cos2A + 2CosASinA – 1)/CosASinA] - 1

⇒ [(1 + 2CosASinA – 1)/CosASinA] - 1 ⇒ [2CosASinA/CosASinA] - 1

⇒ [2] - 1 = 1

questions.question: The expression 3 sec 2 θ tan 2 θ + tan 6 θ – sec 6 θ is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: The expression 3 sec<sup>2</sup> θ tan<sup>2</sup> θ + tan<sup>6</sup> θ – sec<sup>6</sup> θ is equal to:
questions.solution:
3 sec2 θ tan2 θ + tan6 θ – sec6 θ

⇒ 3 sec2 θ tan2 θ + (tan2 θ)3 – (sec2 θ)3

⇒ 3 sec2 θ tan2 θ + (tan2 θ – sec2 θ) (tan4 θ + sec4 θ + tan2 θ sec2 θ)

⇒ 3 sec2 θ tan2 θ + (–1) [tan4 θ + sec4 θ – 2 tan2 θ sec2 θ + 3tan2 θ sec2 θ]

⇒ 3 sec2 θ tan2 θ + (–1) [(tan2 θ – sec2 θ)2 + 3 tan2 θ sec2 θ]

⇒ 3 sec2 θ tan2 θ + (–1) [(–1)2 + 3 sec2 θ tan2 θ]

⇒ 3 sec2 θ tan2 θ + (–1) [1 + 3 sec2 θ tan2 θ]

⇒ 3 sec2 θ tan2 θ – 1 – 3 sec2 θ tan2 θ

⇒ (–1)

questions.question: If cosec θ = 1.25, then \(\frac{{4tan\theta - 5\cos \theta \; + \;1}}{{\sec \theta \; + \;4\cot \theta - 1}} = ?\)
questions.questionHtml: If cosec θ = 1.25, then \(\frac{{4tan\theta - 5\cos \theta \; + \;1}}{{\sec \theta \; + \;4\cot \theta - 1}} = ?\)
questions.solution:
Given:

cosecθ = \(1.25\over100\) = \(5\over4\) 

\(\frac{{4tanθ - 5\cos θ \; + \;1}}{{\sec θ \; + \;4\cot θ - 1}} = ?\)

Formula Used:

Pythagorean theorem

H2 = P2 + B2

Calculation:

cosecθ = \(H\over P\) = \(5\over4\)

H2 = P2 + B2

52 = 42 + B2

B2 = 25 -16 = 9

B = √9 = 3

Now,

\(\frac{{4tanθ - 5\cos θ \; + \;1}}{{\sec θ \; + \;4\cot θ - 1}}\)

⇒ \({{4\times{4\over3}}-{5\times{3\over5}}+1}\over{{5\over3}+4\times{3\over4}-1}\)

⇒​ \({{16\over3}-3+1}\over{{5\over3}+3-1}\) = \((16-9+3)\over(5+9-3)\) = \(10\over11\)

questions.question: If 5 cos 2 θ + 1 = 3 sin 2 θ, 0°< θ < 90°, then what is the value of \(\frac{{tan{\rm{\theta \;}} + {\rm{\;sec\theta }}}}{{cot{\rm{\theta \;}} + {\rm{\;cosec\theta }}}}\) ?
questions.questionHtml: If 5 cos2 θ + 1 = 3 sin2θ, 0°< θ < 90°, then what is the value of \(\frac{{tan{\rm{\theta \;}} + {\rm{\;sec\theta }}}}{{cot{\rm{\theta \;}} + {\rm{\;cosec\theta }}}}\)?
questions.solution:
5 cos2 θ + 1 = 3 sin2 θ

⇒ Put θ = 60

⇒ 5 cos2 60 + 1 = 3 sin2 60

⇒ 5 × 1/4 + 1 = 3 × 3/4

⇒ 5/4 + 1 = 9/4

⇒ 9/4 = 9/4 (satisfied)

Now,

⇒ (tan θ + sec θ)/(cot θ + cosec θ)

⇒ (tan 60 + sec 60)/(cot 60 + cosec 60)

⇒ (√3 + 2)/(1/√3 + 2/√3)

⇒ (√3 + 2)/[(1 + 2)/√3]

⇒ (3 + 2√3)/3

Detailed Method:

⇒ 5 cos2 θ + 1 = 3 sin2 θ

⇒ 5 – 5 sin2 θ + 1 = 3 sin2 θ

⇒ 6 = 8 sin2 θ

⇒ sin2 θ = 6/8

⇒ sin2 θ = 3/4

⇒ sin θ = √3/2

⇒ sin θ = sin 60

⇒ θ = 60

Now,

⇒ (tan θ + sec θ)/(cot θ + cosec θ)

⇒ (tan 60 + sec 60)/(cot 60 + cosec 60)

⇒ (√3 + 2)/(1/√3 + 2/√3)

⇒ (√3 + 2)/[(1 + 2)/√3]

⇒ (3 + 2√3)/3

questions.question: If tan4A = cot(A – 20°), 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of A is:
questions.questionHtml: If tan4A = cot(A – 20°), 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of A is:
questions.solution:
Given :

tan4A = cot(A – 20°)

Formula used :

tanθ = cot (90° – θ)

Calculations :

cot (90° – 4A) = cot (A – 20°)

⇒ 90°– 4A = A – 20° 

⇒ 5A = 110° 

⇒ A = 22° 

∴ The value of A will be 22°

questions.question: Let x = r cos (t), y = r sin (t) cos (u), z = r sin (t)sin (u). Then the value of x 2 + y 2 + z 2 is ___.
questions.questionHtml: Let x = r cos (t), y = r sin (t) cos (u), z = r sin (t)sin (u). Then the value of x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> + z<sup>2</sup> is ___.
questions.solution:
x = r cos(t), y = r sin(t) cos(u), z = r sin(t) sin(u)

⇒ x2 + y2 + z2 = (r cos(t))2 + (r sin(t) cos(u))2 + (r sin(t) sin(u))2

⇒ r2 cos2(t) + r2 sin2(t) cos2(u) + r2 sin2(t) sin2(u)

⇒ r2 (cos2(t) + sin2(t)(cos2(u) + sin2(u)))

⇒ r2 (cos2(t) + sin2(t)) = r2

questions.question: If 3(sec 2 θ + tan 2 θ) = 5, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of cosec θ is:
questions.questionHtml: If 3(sec<sup>2</sup>θ  + tan<sup>2</sup>θ) = 5, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of cosec θ is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut TrickBy observation:

Option (1) and (2) can't be the answer as the value of cosec θ is always greater and equal to 1 or less and equal to -1.

Let cosec θ = 2, θ = 30° 

Put this value in the equation,

3(sec230  + tan230) = 5,

⇒ 3(4/3 + 1/3) = 5 

⇒ 5 = 5

The equation is satisfied.

∴ The value of cosec θ is 2.

Alternate MethodGiven:

3(sec2θ  + tan2θ) = 5

Formula:

sec2θ = 1 + tan2θ

Calculation:

⇒ 3(sec2θ  + tan2θ) = 5

⇒ 3(1 + tan2θ + tan2θ) = 5

⇒ 3 (1 + 2tan2θ) = 5

⇒ θ = 30° as 0° < θ < 90°

Then,

questions.question: if cosec A = 10, then what is the value of 20 sin A + 9 √11 sec A? Given that A is an acute angle.

if cosec A = 10, then what is the value of 20 sin A + 9 √11 sec A?

Given that A is an acute angle.
questions.solution:
Given:

cosec A = 10

Concept used:

H2 = P2 + B2

sinA = P/H, cosA = B/H, sinA = 1/cosecA, cosA = 1/secA

Calculation:

cosec A = 10/1 = H/P

comparing values, H = 10, P = 1 then B = √[H2 - P2] = √[102 - 12]

⇒ B = √99 = 3√11

⇒ 20 sin A + 9 √11 sec A

⇒ 20 × 1/10 + 9 √11 × 10/[3√11]

⇒ 2 + 3 × 10

⇒ 32

questions.question: In ΔABC, right angled at B, if cot C = 3, then \(\frac{{\cos C(\sin C + \sin A)}}{{\sin A(\cos C - \cos A)}}\) is equal to :
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, right angled at B, if cot C = 3, then \(\frac{{\cos C(\sin C + \sin A)}}{{\sin A(\cos C - \cos A)}}\) is equal to :

cot C = 3

Concept used:

Cotθ = Cosθ/Sinθ

Cosθ = B/H

Sinθ = P/H

Calculation:

CosC = 3/√10

SinC = 1/√10

SinA = 3/√10

CosA = 1/√10

So,

\(\frac{{\cos C(\sin C + \sin A)}}{{\sin A(\cos C - \cos A)}}\)

⇒ [3/√10(1/√10 + 3/√10)]/[3/√10(3/√10 - 1/√10)]

⇒ (3/√10 × 4/√10)/(3/√10 × 2/√10)

⇒ 2

∴ Required answer is 2

\(\frac {\sin^2 30^\circ + \cos^2 60^\circ - \sec 35^\circ.\sin 55^\circ}{\sec 60^\circ + \rm cosec\;30^\circ}\)

questions.question: For A = 30°, find the value of: \(\frac{-3\sin^22A+2\sec^2A-\tan\frac{3A}{2}}{\frac{1}{3}\sin3A}\)
questions.questionHtml: For A = 30°, find the value of: \(\frac{-3\sin^22A+2\sec^2A-\tan\frac{3A}{2}}{\frac{1}{3}\sin3A}\)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Substitute A = 30° directly into the given expression.

Numerator = −3×sin260° + 2×sec230° − tan45° = −3×(3/4) + 2×(4/3) − 1 = −7/12.

Denominator = (1/3)×sin90° = 1/3.

Result = (−7/12) ÷ (1/3) = −7/4.

∴ The correct answer is −7/4.

Alternate Method

Given:

A = 30°

Expression: [−3sin22A + 2sec2A − tan(3A/2)] / [(1/3)sin3A]

Calculation:

⇒ Substitute A = 30° into the individual terms:

⇒ sin(2A) = sin(2 × 30°) = sin(60°) = √3/2

⇒ sec(A) = sec(30°) = 2/√3

⇒ tan(3A/2) = tan(3 × 30° / 2) = tan(45°) = 1

⇒ sin(3A) = sin(3 × 30°) = sin(90°) = 1

⇒ Now substitute these values back into the expression:

⇒ Numerator = −3×(√3/2)2 + 2×(2/√3)2 − 1

⇒ Numerator = −3×(3/4) + 2×(4/3) − 1

⇒ Numerator = −9/4 + 8/3 − 1

⇒ LCM of 4 and 3 is 12.

⇒ Numerator = (−27 + 32 − 12) / 12 = −7/12

⇒ Denominator = (1/3) × 1 = 1/3

⇒ Final Value = (−7/12) / (1/3)

⇒ Final Value = (−7/12) × 3 = −7/4

∴ The correct answer is −7/4.

Additional Information

Standard Trigonometric Values

For standard angles: sin(30°) = 1/2, sin(60°) = √3/2, sin(90°) = 1. The tangent of 45° is always 1.

Reciprocal Identities

sec(θ) = 1/cos(θ), cosec(θ) = 1/sin(θ), and cot(θ) = 1/tan(θ). Since cos(30°) = √3/2, sec(30°) = 2/√3.

Basic Trigonometric Identities

sin2(θ) + cos2(θ) = 1, 1 + tan2(θ) = sec2(θ), and 1 + cot2(θ) = cosec2(θ).

questions.question: The elimination of θ from xcos θ - ysinθ = 2 and xsinθ + ycosθ = 4 will give:
questions.questionHtml: The elimination of θ from xcos θ - ysinθ = 2 and xsinθ + ycosθ = 4 will give:
questions.solution:
Given : 

xcosθ - ysinθ = 2 

xsinθ + ycosθ = 4 

Formula used: 

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1

(a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab

Calculation: 

xcosθ - ysinθ = 2 

On squaring we get,

⇒ x2cos2θ + y2sin2θ – 2(xcosθ)(ysinθ) = 4      ….(i)

xsinθ + ycosθ = 4 

On squaring we get,

⇒ x2sin2θ + y2cos2θ + 2(ycosθ)(xsinθ) = 16      ….(ii)

On adding eqns (i) and (ii)

⇒ x2cos2θ + y2sin2θ – 2(xcosθ)(ysinθ) + x2sin2θ + y2cos2θ + 2(ycosθ)(xsinθ) = 4 + 16

⇒ x2(cos2θ + sin2θ) + y2(sin2θ + cos2θ) = 20

⇒ x2 + y2 = 20

∴ The correct answer is x2 + y2 = 20

questions.question: If cotθ = √11 , then the value of \(\frac{cosec^{2}θ - sec^{2}θ}{cosec^2θ + sec^2θ}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If cotθ = √11 , then the value of \(\frac{cosec^{2}θ - sec^{2}θ}{cosec^2θ + sec^2θ}\) is:
questions.solution:
cotθ = √11

⇒ sec2θ = 1 + tan2θ = 1 + (1/√11)2 = 1 + 1/11 = 12/11

questions.question: Find the value of the following expression. (1 + tan θ + sec θ) × ( 1 + cot θ - cosec θ)
questions.questionHtml:
Find the value of the following expression.

(1 + tan θ + sec θ) × ( 1 + cot θ - cosec θ)
questions.solution:
Given:

(1 + tan θ + sec θ) × (1 + cot θ - cosec θ)

Formula used:

tan θ = sin θ / cos θ

sec θ = 1 / cos θ

cot θ = cos θ / sin θ

cosec θ = 1 / sin θ

Calculation:

(1 + tan θ + sec θ) × (1 + cot θ - cosec θ)

⇒ (1 + sin θ / cos θ + 1 / cos θ) × (1 + cos θ / sin θ - 1 / sin θ)

⇒ (1 + (sin θ + 1) / cos θ) × (1 + (cos θ - 1) / sin θ)

⇒ (cos θ + sin θ + 1) / cos θ × (sin θ + cos θ - 1) / sin θ

⇒ [(cos θ + sin θ + 1) × (sin θ + cos θ - 1)] / (cos θ × sin θ)

Expanding the numerator:

⇒ (cos² θ + cos θ sin θ - cos θ + sin θ cos θ + sin² θ - sin θ + cos θ + sin θ - 1)

⇒ (cos² θ + sin² θ + 2 cos θ sin θ - 1)

Using the Pythagorean identity, cos² θ + sin² θ = 1:

⇒ (1 + 2 cos θ sin θ - 1)

⇒ 2 cos θ sin θ

Thus, the expression simplifies to:

⇒ 2 cos θ sin θ / (cos θ sin θ)

⇒ 2

∴ The correct answer is option (3).
